fact_text: Short selling means selling first and buying back later, so the profit comes from a price that falls; it is used mostly in falling markets.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Introduction to Short Selling in PMEX | Commodity Market Strategies | Pakistan Mercantile Exchange' (YouTube, 2025-05-08)

fact_text: Profit on a short sale equals the sell price minus the buy-back price; the analyst's example of selling gold at 2,100 and buying back at 1,900 gave 200 dollars.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Introduction to Short Selling in PMEX | Commodity Market Strategies | Pakistan Mercantile Exchange' (YouTube, 2025-05-08)

fact_text: PMEX allows short selling in every commodity it lists, with initial and maintenance margin requirements the same as in normal trading.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Introduction to Short Selling in PMEX | Commodity Market Strategies | Pakistan Mercantile Exchange' (YouTube, 2025-05-08)

fact_text: Gold was in an uptrend against the US dollar from 4 Oct 2023 on the analyst's daily chart, so buyers from that period were in profit.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Introduction to Short Selling in PMEX | Commodity Market Strategies | Pakistan Mercantile Exchange' (YouTube, 2025-05-08)

fact_text: Gold fell steadily from a Sep 2011 high to a Dec 2015 low, a downtrend of about four years in which buyers during that period were at a loss.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Introduction to Short Selling in PMEX | Commodity Market Strategies | Pakistan Mercantile Exchange' (YouTube, 2025-05-08)

fact_text: A downtrend is when price makes lower highs and lower lows, and falls more than it rises over the period.
source_name: Standard Capital Securities, 'Introduction to Short Selling in PMEX | Commodity Market Strategies | Pakistan Mercantile Exchange' (YouTube, 2025-05-08)
